exposure: Neonates born by C-section from Cluster I mothers
Maternal microbial clusters (Cluster I - Prevotella dominant, Cluster II - Ruminococcus dominant)
Maternal dietary intake (total dietary fiber, omega-3 fatty acids, polyphenols)
finding: Maternal diet during pregnancy, particularly fiber, lipid, and protein intake, influences maternal gut microbiota composition, which in turn affects neonatal gut microbiota and infant growth trajectories, with C-section neonates from mothers with a Prevotella-dominant gut microbiota showing an increased risk of overweight at 18 months.
mod_finding: Birth mode (vaginal vs. C-section) interacted with maternal microbial clusters to influence infant growth trajectories.
